worked_solution:
An expression is a tautology if it is always true, regardless of the inputs.

By completing the final column in the truth table below, we obtain the following:

| $\,X\,$ | $\,Y\,$ | $\,X∧¬Y\,$ | $\,X⇒Y\,$ | $\,(X∧¬Y)∨(X⇒Y)\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |

According to the table, $(X∧¬Y)∨(X⇒Y)$ 
$\text{is}$
always true. Therefore, it 
$\text{is}$
a tautology.
